newsitem.title: GERMANY: ATHLETICS-KUZENKOVA SMASHES HAMMER WORLD RECORD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KUZENKOVA SMASHES HAMMER WORLD RECORD.

text.p: Olga Kuzenkova of Russia twice smashed the women's world hammer record, breaking the 70-metre barrier at the European Cup final on Sunday.
Kuzenkova's best throw of 73.10 metres added nearly four metres to the previous best of 69.58 set by Mihaela Melinte of Romania in Bucharest in March. The Russian achieved 71.22 in her first throw.
Melinte had to settle for second place despite breaking her own old record with a throw of 69.76.
Kuzenkova has been expecting for more than a month to become the first woman to break the 70-metre barrier.
"At the end of May I surpassed 70 metres for the first time," she said. "It wasn't measured but it was clear that it was well over 70 metres."
Kuzenkova's performance was even more remarkable, given the wet conditions in Munich's Olympic stadium.
"Sometimes it is an excuse for some men if they don't achieve their performances due to rain and the wet," she said. "Women simply have more endurance."
Jonathan Edwards of Britain was also on form in the early events on the second day of the competition.
The world triple jump record holder leaped 17.74 metres in the second round, the longest jump in the world this year.
Edwards decided not to make any further attempts because of the cold and the rain.
Christine Arron of France proved to be a more than able substitute for Olympic champion Marie-Jose Perec in the women's 200 metres.
Perec decided late on Friday not to compete but compatriot Arron still took maximum points, winning in 22.89 seconds.
The poor conditions meant that the men's pole vault was moved into a nearby sports hall. It was the first time in European Cup history that the event had to be held indoors.
